subject: Intermittent token timeouts — asymmetric routing suspicion
messages:
From: Aaron Cho <netops@finserve.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 401s / TLS resets to Redwood private agent (on-prem)

Hi Vivek —

We're seeing intermittent 401s and occasional TLS resets when our internal services call the Redwood agent deployed in our data center (agent v1.3.2). The requests come from multiple app servers but only a subset of requests fail, and failures correlate with the following:

- client IPs observed in your logs (x.x.x.10/11) don't always match the source we see on the backend (x.x.x.200+).
- tcpdump on the agent host shows incoming SYNs from the app pool, but replies appear to go out via a different egress IP (we suspect asymmetric routing via F5 -> Internet -> NAT gateway).

Attached a short pcap (tcpdump_snip.pcap) and a stripped NAT translation log excerpt. Example symptom: repeated token validation errors immediately after connections which appear to resume without config changes.

We tried pinning stickiness on the F5 for a subset of flows for 30m and saw improvements, but it came back after translations expired. Can you advise whether your agent expects symmetric L3/L4 path (same src/dst IPs/ports) for token/session validation?

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Cho
Platform Network Engineer — FinServe

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cho <netops@finserve.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 401s / TLS resets to Redwood private agent (on-prem)

Hi Aaron —

Thanks for the packet and logs — confirmed receipt. Short answer: yes, asymmetric NAT/egress behavior can cause the symptoms you describe. A few notes up front:

- Redwood's private agent uses TLS session resumption and token-based auth tied to the connection 5-tuple in some flows. If the return path SNATs replies to a different external IP (or changes source port pools), the client’s socket and server’s view can diverge, leading to session failures or what looks like a 401 when the handshake/token exchange is disrupted.
- Agent v1.3.2 doesn't actively rebind tokens when the source IP observed by the token issuer changes mid-session. v1.4 includes a short-term mitigation (session affinity via keepalives) that helps with brief stickiness lapses.

Immediate ask: can you run the following so we can confirm asymmetric routing and NAT timeouts?
1) tcpdump on agent host for 10 minutes: tcpdump -i eth0 host <app-ip> and attach a few MB of capture.
2) show conntrack | grep <app-ip> (or tmsh nat translation list) from your F5/NAT box at the time of a failed request.
3) curl -v --resolve agent.redwood.local:443:<agent-ip> https://agent.redwood.local/healthz from an affected app node and paste the TLS client hello/server response when failure occurs.

Temporary mitigations to try while we investigate:
- Configure SNAT persistence on your F5 for the app-to-agent flows (stick to a small pool or single translation IP).
- Add a route so replies to the app subnet follow the same next-hop (source-based routing / policy) to avoid hairpinning to a different egress.

I'll loop in Jonas to provide the conntrack/NAT checks and a possible packet-level explanation. We'll also schedule a quick debug window if you can provide a 30-minute slot.

Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aaron Cho <netops@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 401s / TLS resets to Redwood private agent (on-prem)

Quick diagnostic checklist from my side:

- On the agent host: netstat -tnp | grep 443 and ss -tn state established to correlate socket tuples to your app IPs. If established sockets flip endpoints mid-life that's a red flag.
- On F5 / NAT: 
  * show conntrack (Linux) or tmsh show /ltm nat translations (F5) around the failure timestamps. Look for NAT entries for the same source IP mapping to multiple SNAT pools.
  * Check SNAT automap vs. NAT pools: automap will pick available IPs and can rotate if pool exhaustion or idle timeouts vary.
- Check for ECMP/BGP asymmetry: traceroute from app -> agent and traceroute agent -> app; compare AS path and next-hops.

Hypothesis: Your F5 is using a SNAT pool with multiple addresses and stickiness TTL shorter than the token/session window. When a client's connection is routed back via a different egress IP, the agent sees a new source and treats the TLS/token exchange as invalid.

If you can forward the small pcap and the nat-translation-log.txt (timestamps especially), I can correlate the exact packet sequence. Also please capture a short flow while reproducing a failure with tcpdump -w /tmp/flow.pcap host <app-ip> and a simultaneous tcpdump on the F5 if possible.

Jonas Weber
Support Engineer — Networks
Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Cho <netops@finserve.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 401s / TLS resets to Redwood private agent (on-prem)

Update after running your checks: we captured conntrack dumps and a second pcap during a reproducer. Key findings:

- Conntrack shows the source (10.45.12.7) mapping to SNAT pool IPs 35.199.12.5 and 35.199.12.9 depending on time. The entries that rotated correlate with failed requests.
- The pcap shows SYN from app -> agent (35.199.12.5), agent SYN/ACK, then a retransmit where the reply took the path via 35.199.12.9, causing the client's TLS handshake to abort in our app and subsequently a 401-ish token error.
- We temporarily forced a static SNAT for the app subnet to 35.199.12.5 — errors stopped for ~3 hours, then started again after an internal process on the F5 recycled translations (we suspect a TTL + connection reuse behavior).

Attached nat-translation-log.txt and a short excerpt. We're open to a debug window; however, this looks like a config mismatch on our side. We have two options we want guidance on:

1) Redwood side: is there a recommended agent config (v1.3.2) we can set to be tolerant of short SNAT rotations (e.g., accept resumed sessions with different SNAT IP within a grace window), or schedule upgrade to v1.4 which includes keepalive affinity changes?
2) Our side: implement a permanent static 1:1 NAT or increase stickiness TTL for the SNAT pool.

Thanks for the fast responses.

—Aaron

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cho <netops@finserve.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 401s / TLS resets to Redwood private agent (on-prem)

Aaron —

Appreciate the captures and the quick mitigation test. Summary and recommended next steps:

What happened: asymmetric egress/NAT rotation caused source IP churn for legitimate app sessions. Agent behavior + token/session window resulted in transient failures when the return path used a different SNAT address.

Short-term recommendations (apply now):
- Implement static 1:1 SNAT for the affected app subnet to a single egress IP (your test showed this removed errors).
- Increase SNAT persistence TTL for the NAT pool to be longer than your token/session TTLs.
- If static SNAT is not possible, keep F5 stickiness but reserve a small, single-address pool for Redwood agent flows.

Medium-term (engineering / cross-team):
- Redwood: we will prioritize backporting a session-resilience patch into the next point release (v1.3.x) to tolerate very short-lived SNAT IP changes for token refresh windows. The patch is a mitigation only — not a replacement for correct symmetric routing.
- FinServe: consider a routing policy to avoid hairpinned egress for data-center-to-data-center flows (source-based route or ensuring return path via same egress).

Operational next steps:
- I will open a Jira (NET-2345) with the captures and a proposed playbook (support_playbook-asym-route.md) describing diagnostics and recommended firewall/NAT configs.
- Suggest a 60-minute maintenance window this week where Redwood can join and watch a live repro while you apply a permanent SNAT change. Please propose 2 slots and we'll coordinate.

I'll leave the ticket open and will copy our product reliability lead if we need to escalate to an agent code fix. Thanks again for the detailed traces — that made root cause fast to identify.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
